hotspots.label: Root system
hotspots.copy: Primary and lateral roots branch into fine absorbing roots that anchor the plant, acquire water and ions, respire, and interact with the rhizosphere.

hotspots.label: Stem & vascular system
hotspots.detail: Main stem, branches, xylem & phloem pathway
hotspots.copy: The main stem and branches form a continuous vascular skeleton. Xylem moves water and minerals; phloem redistributes sugars and other assimilates among sources and sinks.

hotspots.label: Nodes, meristems & branching
hotspots.copy: Nodes carry leaves, branches, and axillary meristems. Their spacing and bud activity reveal how growth regulators and environment shape plant architecture.

hotspots.label: Fan leaves
hotspots.detail: Serrated leaflets, petioles, midribs & lateral veins
hotspots.copy: Serrated leaflets connect through petioles to the vascular system. Midribs and lateral veins distribute water, minerals, sugars, and mechanical support through the blade.

hotspots.label: Flowers & inflorescences
hotspots.copy: Layered bracts, sugar leaves, stigmas, and dense glandular surfaces form the visible inflorescence. Floral structure changes through pollination and maturation.

hotspots.label: Glandular trichomes
hotspots.copy: Glandular trichomes include stalks, secretory disc cells, and gland heads. Their form and density vary by tissue, developmental stage, and genotype.

hotspots.label: Reproductive structures
hotspots.copy: Stigmas and preflowers connect visible floral anatomy to sex expression, pollen reception, fertilization, embryo development, and seed formation.
